basis: Clonal histiocytic neoplasm; destructive bone lesions ~70%, skin infiltration ~50%, and liver involvement ~30-40% in multisystem cases.

decisions.hepatic: involved: direct hepatic infiltration occurs in approximately 30-40% of multisystem cases.

basis: ID, myopathy and calcified pinnae define syndrome; hearing loss 12/14; cataracts 80-99%. Hypogonadism and anemia, each HPO 80-99%, omitted at cap.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: myopathy is named in the syndrome synonym; progressive muscle wasting and contractures are characteristic structural manifestations.
decisions.otologic: primary: calcified external ears are defining; hearing impairment occurs in 12/14 patients (~86%).

basis: Autoinflammation with defining deafness; uveitis and arthritis each HPO 80-99%. Rash is transient; renal AA amyloidosis is separate. Cranial neuropathy omitted at cap.

decisions.renal: none: renal AA amyloidosis is annotated at 30-79%, but represents a separately diagnosed secondary disease.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: inflammatory arthritis is annotated at 80-99%, supporting common direct joint involvement.

basis: Constitutional DNA repair cancer-predisposition syndrome; hematologic, brain and intestinal cancers are separate diseases whose risk is increased.

decisions.haematologic: none: predisposition to leukemia or lymphoma does not establish existing blood or marrow disease.
decisions.gastrointestinal: none: increased risk of intestinal polyposis and colon cancer does not establish intrinsic gastrointestinal damage.
decisions.neurologic: none: brain tumors are separate diseases within the predisposition spectrum, not established neurologic damage from this syndrome.

basis: Benign capillary-vessel neoplasm; cutaneous and subcutaneous tumor occupation occurs in most typical presentations (>50%), despite the umbrella including other sites.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: skin or subcutaneous tumor occupation occurs in most typical cases, exceeding 30%; this is direct local tumor involvement.

basis: Bardet-Biedl spectrum: retinal dystrophy, obesity/hypogonadism and polydactyly define disease; renal abnormalities ~30-50%. Cognitive impairment (~60%) omitted at cap.

decisions.neurologic: none at cap: cognitive impairment occurs in roughly 60% of the Bardet-Biedl spectrum; retain defining retinal, endocrine, skeletal and renal disease.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: postaxial polydactyly is a major Bardet-Biedl diagnostic criterion, occurring in roughly 70-80%.

basis: Disease is located in the renal artery, a cardiovascular structure; intrinsic kidney damage is not established across this umbrella.

decisions.renal: none: renal arterial location alone does not establish kidney parenchymal disease; common direct renal damage is not demonstrated.

basis: Marrow hypocellularity 2/2; biliary atresia, esophageal atresia and primum ASD each 1/2. Absent thumb (1/2) omitted at cap in favor of visceral defects; very small sample.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: primum atrial septal defect occurs in 1/2 reported patients (50%); prioritize this potentially serious cardiac defect under the cap.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none at cap: absent thumb occurs in 1/2 patients (50%), but marrow disease and potentially severe hepatic, gastrointestinal and cardiac defects take priority.

basis: Spastic paraplegia and retinal degeneration define the syndrome; retinal degeneration occurs in 3/7 (~43%). Neurogenic bladder symptoms do not establish direct urinary injury.

decisions.ocular: primary: retinal degeneration is explicitly part of the disease definition and syndrome synonyms; documented in 3/7 patients (~43%).

basis: Skin lesions, odontogenic jaw keratocysts and characteristic skeletal anomalies define PTCH1-related Gorlin syndrome; rib anomalies occur in ~50-60%. Falx calcification is non-damaging.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: bifid, fused or markedly splayed ribs are major diagnostic criteria; characteristic skeletal anomalies are intrinsic to the syndrome.
